fx.income.not-loaded: Income is not calculated yet. Prices and costs are not loaded.
fx.twins.not-loaded: Similar fields are not loaded yet.
fx.history.none: No crop history is available for this field. Enter your last crops by hand.
fx.basis.indicator.strong: All inputs for this indicator are present. The range is 8% either side of the score.
fx.basis.indicator.moderate: One input is missing or comes from a nearby point. The range is 15% either side of the score, a rule of thumb.
fx.basis.indicator.weak: Two or more inputs are missing. The range is 25% either side of the score, a rule of thumb.
fx.basis.soil-health: Mean of the four soil indicators with equal weights. The range is the mean of their ranges.
fx.basis.climate: Share of crop years without damaging drought, heat or frost. The range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile year of the {years} years on record at this field.
fx.basis.climate.weak: One crop in this rotation has no tested limits near this field, so the range over the {years} years on record is wide.
fx.basis.water: Share of crop years, out of {years}, in which rain covered what the crops need.
fx.basis.forage: Share of rotation years that produce forage. A cover crop that can be grazed or cut counts as half a year.
fx.basis.total: Soil health counts for {soil}%, climate resilience for {climate}% and your priorities for {priorities}%.
fx.evidence.legume-years: A legume grows in {legumeYears} of the {years} rotation years.
fx.evidence.cover-months: In each {total}-month cycle the crop calendar shows {bare} bare months and {living} months with a living crop or cover crop.
fx.why.current: This is the rotation the field grows now. Every other option is compared with it.
fx.why.legume: Soybean fixes nitrogen that the next maize crop can use.
fx.why.rye-cover: Cereal rye keeps living roots in the soil over winter, after the maize is harvested.
fx.why.small-change: It is the smallest change from what you grow now. The cash crops stay the same.
fx.why.small-grain: Winter wheat adds a third crop family and breaks the maize and soybean pest cycle.
fx.why.summer-window: Wheat comes off in July, which leaves time to spread manure or sow a cover crop.
fx.why.perennial: Two years of alfalfa keep the soil covered all year and build organic matter.
fx.why.alfalfa-nitrogen: Alfalfa leaves nitrogen for the maize that follows it.
fx.why.forage: Oats and alfalfa produce forage in three years out of five.
fx.why.soybean-drought: Soybean copes with a dry July better than maize, so fewer crop years are lost to drought.
fx.why.lower-water: Two soybean years need less water than two maize years would.
fx.why.winter-cover: Winter crops cover the soil from autumn to harvest, so no month is left bare.
fx.why.pea-nitrogen: Field pea fixes nitrogen that the winter wheat after it can use.
fx.why.mustard-cover: White mustard covers the soil between wheat harvest and pea sowing.
fx.why.four-year: Rapeseed returns every fourth year instead of every third.
fx.why.diverse: Five crops from four families give every pest and disease a long break.
fx.why.pea-before-rapeseed: Field pea fixes nitrogen that the rapeseed after it can use.
fx.why.spring-crops: Two spring crops break the disease cycle of winter cereals.
fx.why.root-crop: Potato adds a root crop from a family the field has not grown.
fx.why.rye-hardy: Rye handles dry springs and hard frost better than wheat on light soil.
fx.why.low-water-crops: All three crops need little water.
fx.benefit.known-system: You already have the equipment, the buyers and the experience.
fx.benefit.legume-credit: Soybean lowers the nitrogen fertiliser the maize needs.
fx.benefit.living-roots: The soil has living roots through the winter after maize.
fx.benefit.nitrate-kept: Rye takes up nitrate that would otherwise wash out over winter.
fx.benefit.pest-break: Maize rootworm and soybean cyst nematode go one more year without a host.
fx.benefit.workload: Field work is spread over more of the year.
fx.benefit.less-erosion: Less soil is open to spring rain.
fx.benefit.forage-supply: The rotation produces hay in two years out of five.
fx.benefit.fewer-drought-losses: Fewer crop years are hit by drought in the {years}-year record.
fx.benefit.winter-cover: The soil is covered through winter.
fx.benefit.less-fertiliser: The wheat after pea needs less nitrogen fertiliser.
fx.benefit.disease-break: Related crops return less often, so their diseases get a longer break.
fx.benefit.spread-risk: A bad year for one crop touches one fifth of the rotation.
fx.benefit.low-cost: Rye needs less fertiliser and spraying than wheat.
fx.gap.soc-map: Soil organic carbon comes from a soil survey map unit, not from a sample of this field.
fx.gap.soc-grid: Soil organic carbon comes from a 250 m map, not from a sample of this field.
fx.gap.history-source: Crop history comes from a 30 m satellite map, not from your records.
fx.gap.rye-after-soybean: We did not test rye after soybean as well, which would cover the months that stay bare.
fx.gap.weak.wheat-record: Winter wheat is rare near this field, so its frost and heat limits are not tested here. Treat the climate score as uncertain.
fx.gap.long-fallow: After wheat harvest the calendar shows no crop until maize planting. We did not test a cover crop in that window.
fx.gap.alfalfa-establishment: We did not check whether alfalfa establishes on this field's drainage class.
fx.gap.below-floor: Soil health is more than {points} points below your current rotation, so this option is not offered when you rank on keeping the soil.
fx.gap.nematode-not-checked: We did not check soybean cyst nematode pressure on this field.
fx.gap.slope-missing: Slope is not loaded for this field, so the erosion score uses soil cover only.
fx.gap.pea-dry-spring: We did not check pea yields in dry springs on this soil.
fx.gap.beet-water: We did not check whether sugar beet gets enough water here without irrigation.
fx.gap.weak.potato-inputs: Slope and the drought limits for potato are missing for this field. Treat the scores as uncertain.
fx.gap.bare-after-potato: After potato harvest the calendar shows bare soil until spring. We did not test a cover crop there.
fx.risk.winter-bare: The soil is open from soybean harvest to maize planting. Check your slopes for erosion after spring rain.
fx.risk.two-crop-pests: Check with your advisor for rootworm and nematode build-up in a two-crop rotation.
fx.risk.rye-termination: Check with your advisor that rye can be terminated before soybean planting in a wet spring.
fx.risk.rye-seed-cost: Check the cost of rye seed and of terminating it against your budget.
fx.risk.wheat-market: Check with your advisor whether winter wheat has a buyer within hauling distance.
fx.risk.winterkill: Ask neighbours how often winter wheat survives a winter without snow cover here.
fx.risk.hay-market: Check whether you have livestock or a hay buyer for two years of alfalfa.
fx.risk.hay-equipment: Check that you own or can hire hay equipment.
fx.risk.soybean-after-soybean: Check with your advisor before growing soybean after soybean. Disease and nematodes build up.
fx.risk.low-residue: Soybean leaves little residue. Check the erosion risk on your slopes.
fx.risk.rapeseed-interval: Rapeseed returns every third year. Check with your advisor for clubroot.
fx.risk.cereal-disease: Wheat in two years out of three raises the risk of take-all. Check your fields.
fx.risk.pea-market: Check with your advisor whether field pea has a buyer within hauling distance.
fx.risk.mustard-clubroot: White mustard is in the same family as rapeseed. Ask your advisor whether phacelia is safer here.
fx.risk.beet-contract: Sugar beet needs a contract with a sugar factory. Check whether one near you takes new growers.
fx.risk.beet-harvest: A late beet harvest can compact wet soil. Check with your advisor.
fx.risk.potato-irrigation: Potato on light soil often needs irrigation. Check your access to water.
fx.risk.potato-storage: Check whether you have storage or a buyer at harvest.
fx.risk.cereal-only: Three cereal years in a row raise disease and weed pressure. Check with your advisor.
fx.risk.rye-price: Rye usually sells for less than wheat. Check prices with your buyer.
